approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted, scored molecules. It samples breeding parents from high-scoring bands, recombines connected fragments and applies local mutations, including occasional successive mutations. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is already disabled. Stable canonical identity checks admit a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process trained only on earlier accepted observations uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity. Correlated posterior score draws select one available pool member at each batch position; real accepted feedback then updates both the full prediction archive and the bounded breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove sampled residual influence from successful allocation by choosing candidates in stable decreasing posterior-mean order. Keep the count model, covariance, factorization and the original random draws as passive comparators. This repeats a specific component removal on the current exchange-free Parent, where its endpoint contribution is unresolved; the earlier mean-only control used an exchange-enabled search and lost endpoint score. There are no evaluated children of the supplied Parent in this brief. The separately registered correlation control retains nonzero residual influence, whereas this experiment removes that influence entirely. The prediction is a material endpoint loss if exploratory choices still sustain useful search paths.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting uncertainty in n-62daf219c70a is its unisolated dependence on sampled departures from the learned mean after the graph menu changed. Its actual three summary.json and run.log files report complete successful panels: macro mean 0.5956696497334577, population SD 0.02659287062806747, and seed macros 0.625411930168826, 0.560865654270234 and 0.600731364761313. The indexed full activation report records substantial task dispersion and 435 retained count-posterior batches. A read-only audit of all fifteen actual task logs finds 4,350 successful sampled choices, 3,755 strict departures from the available posterior-mean maximizer, changed mean-ranked order in all 435 batches and changed selected sets with a strict total-mean gap in 432 batches. There are no selection-reconstruction failures or numerical fallbacks; all 870 training/pool factorizations succeed. These are genuine exposed allocation differences, not evidence that sampled excursions are waste. The prior removal n-852bc7be4d7c above n-559d25e9c9c7 followed mean order for every choice and lost 0.040407162268268314 in paired macro score, with all three seed macros declining, despite parent-beating offspring increasing from 624 to 707 and selected-stream prediction MSE falling. Its same-pool nonempty core count fell from 6.503 to 4.437 per batch, and accepted batch-best fell from 0.487313 to 0.437676. That is conditional support for sampled residual influence, not a current effect estimate. Historical exchange removal n-c55c3d520a2c changed the graph menu and improved its mean contrary to its registered loss prediction; the current same-code baseline reproduces it without adding independent trajectories. Therefore neither the old residual benefit nor favorable local yields settle the present contribution question. The resource warning in the Parent logs is retained as provenance; supplied Slurm accounting confirms the three formal steps completed with the frozen allocation, so the warning alone is not evidence of a profile mismatch.
hypothesis: Remove sampled residual influence on successful pool allocation by selecting each available candidate with the highest original posterior mean, resolving exact ties by increasing pool index, while retaining the inherited full count posterior and correlated sampled arrays as passive controls.

finding_summary.headline: Mean-only selection executed and reduced the final mean by 0.076861
finding_summary.insights: Sampled departures from the learned mean support the endpoint score in this exchange-free composition. More local successes did not compensate for losing them: parent-beating offspring rose from 629 to 698, more survivors bred again, and prediction MSE fell from 0.012718 to 0.004033 while every seed macro worsened. Those proxies therefore cannot replace the endpoint test. Lower uncertainty exposure and narrower selected families fit the loss, but their mediation is not isolated, and this removal does not identify the separate value of residual correlation. The chemistry also resists a simple quality verdict: tiny-fragment output almost disappeared and some conventional leaders improved, while elaborate aromatic families, reactive bond environments and unresolved ring geometry persisted. The result supports conditional residual-sampling benefit, with the three endpoint gains and contrary batch-level coverage changes preserved.

molecular.headline: Aromatic families persist, with N-halogenated indoles, oxygen-chain growth, unusual sulfur centres and dense nitrogen bridges
molecular.overall_character: All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectory files were present and read, covering Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 for all five tasks. Each task has 900 records and 870 optimizer proposals; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. The brief identifies n-62daf219c70a as the code Parent and reports both child_complete and paired_complete, with all supplied seeds matched and no profile mismatch. Chemistry comparisons therefore use the complete current-profile Parent panel. This report describes output associations; it does not decide whether the registered mean-only intervention activated or attribute any individual chemical change to a component. The emitted molecules are overwhelmingly ring-bearing and aromatic: both string incidences are 0.9989 or 1.0 across tasks. Those values indicate presence in a molecule, not ring counts, ring diversity or aromatic-atom fraction. Indole amides/amidines, fused nitrogen-rich diones, aryl-containing amines, crowded bridged nitrogen rings and fluorinated heterocycles remain central. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout, despite visible protonatable amines and potential stereogenic centres. Within-seed leaders often retain a family while altering substituents, but distinct seed families remain, supporting moderate overall diversity rather than total collapse. Questionable bond environments persist: N-halogen attachments, consecutive oxygen bonds, unusual sulfur-carbon multiple bonds and dense ring junctions. The Child also contains conventional indole anilides, sulfinamides and an N-F-free fluorinated nitrogen/oxygen ring leader; it is not uniformly chemically implausible. The Parent's tiny-fragment problem is much less conspicuous here: all optimizer proposals in three tasks have ring and aromatic text features. This is a counterexample to carrying a universal ring-loss diagnosis forward unchanged. The most elaborate oxygen-rich leader and the more highly bridged dicarbonyl leader are larger than their matched Parent leaders, yet their score directions differ. Lower scores cannot be equated with worse chemistry, and higher scores do not certify feasibility. Heavy-atom sizes below were counted from cited trajectory SMILES tokens; descriptor models and synthesis validation were not performed. The digest final excerpts are late seed-2 proposals, not every seed's incumbent. Published Parent trajectories support the Parent comparisons; cited_smiles contains only molecules allowed by the current digest or trusted citation paths.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader has 25 heavy atoms and a methoxy/methyl/halomethyl indole with an N-H ring nitrogen, linked through an N-fluorinated amidine to a phenol ring. Chloromethyl, fluoromethyl and bromomethyl versions share the best supplied score. Seed 0 favors an N-halogenated acylhydrazide linking indole and fluorophenyl; seed 2 favors an indole anilide bearing hydroxymethyl and an N-methyl-N-halo amino substituent. Mean proposal SMILES length is 44.9 and halogen incidence is 0.9931. The familiar indole/aryl frameworks are synthetically recognizable, but much of the leading local nitrogen chemistry remains reactive or unusual. Unlike the Parent seed-1 leader, the Child keeps N-H at the indole nitrogen and puts the halogen on the linker nitrogen; this redistributes the concern rather than eliminating it.
liabilities: Leading amidine, hydrazide and pendant amino groups carry N-F, N-Cl or N-Br bonds. An N-H indole ring does not make the entire structure free of reactive nitrogen-halogen chemistry.
Halomethyl groups, N-N linkages and unassigned configurations of imino groups require stability and identity assessment; neither sanitization nor score supplies it.
missing_features: Stable linker alternatives retaining the favorable compact indole/aryl organization at the leading score are not demonstrated; a conventional anilide already performs reasonably well, so the output does not lack ordinary amide chemistry.
Independent compact scaffold arrangements are limited among the leaders compared with their many halogen and short-side-chain variants.
The visible gradients do not identify a missing exact pharmacophore or justify adding halogens indiscriminately.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The three seed-1 halomethyl amidines score 0.42762099872850584, while a methylamide lacking the pendant aromatic region scores 0.038637376887767166 and difluorobenzene scores 2.2064040954992307e-13. The positive association is a combined indole/linker/aryl arrangement; fluorination alone is insufficient. A conventional N-H indole anilide with hydroxymethyl and only a carbon-bound aryl chlorine still scores 0.3940393921126993, so N-halogen chemistry is not universally required. The Child seed-0 hydrazide leader scores 0.40497388700123543 versus the Parent's cumulene-containing leader at 0.39405142067435733, a counterexample to uniform loss. The Child seed-1 and seed-2 leaders score 0.42762099872850584 and 0.4163503402962837, below their respective Parent leaders at 0.47411701813450596 and 0.438972502037081. These are descriptive scaffold associations, not isolated functional-group effects.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 leader has 46 heavy atoms and combines linked aza-aromatic rings with a fused N-methyl dione, ester and butyl substituents, and an alkenyl substituent bearing consecutive oxygen atoms. Many tied leaders elaborate this oxygen chain or exchange ester, thione and short alkyl decorations on the same organization. Seed 0 reaches a 65-heavy-atom assembly of aza-aromatic rings, a fused dione, numerous acyl/ester connections and oxygen-rich peripheral groups. Seed 1 reaches a 39-heavy-atom dione/azaaryl/phenyl assembly with an imidate and a flexible alternating carbon-sulfur chain. Mean proposal SMILES length is 79.3; every proposal has ring and aromatic text features. These are extensively decorated aromatic assemblies, not a failure to build rings. The oxygen-chain and acyl-rich output is substantially less conventional than its recognizable heteroaromatic cores.
liabilities: Consecutive oxygen bonds appear in the leading alkenyl substituent and related acyl-linked decorations. These peroxide or longer oxygen-chain environments warrant a substantial stability concern.

The very large seed-0 leader combines many potentially labile acyl/oxygen connections, while the seed-1 chain adds flexible thioether units. These are different liabilities; the alternating carbon-sulfur chain should not be mistaken for an S-S polysulfide.
Repeated score ties do not validate chemical stability or indicate that progressively more elaborate peripheral groups are useful.
missing_features: The leaders do not demonstrate compact, chemically independent reorganizations that preserve favorable heteroaromatic/carbonyl relationships while avoiding long oxygen-rich or acyl-rich appendages.
Stable peripheral replacements retaining the observed core arrangement are not established at the same score; many distinct reactive decorations receive indistinguishable scores.
The Parent's stronger compact family is not represented among the Child leaders, but this does not identify a mandatory target-specific scaffold or prove the generator cannot construct one.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted dione scores 0.548381482770623 and a compact azaaryl/dione proposal scores 0.5385026737967915. The seed-2 leader reaches 0.5989554700384827; fifteen proposals in that seed share this score despite changes in peripheral oxygen-chain length, ester alkyl groups or carbonyl/thione choices. Thus these local elaborations repeatedly preserve a score plateau rather than demonstrate additional reward. The final variant with another oxygen-rich ester scores 0.5963571703191081. Child seed leaders score 0.5952196819565954, 0.5787542053216435 and 0.5989554700384827, compared with Parent 0.8561477222467935, 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013. In seed 0 the Parent leader is a compact 30-heavy-atom linked heterocycle while the Child leader has 65 heavy atoms. That comparison supports a missing alternative core organization among the current leaders, not a general rule that smaller is always better. No optimizer proposal here is a ringless floor fragment.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 leader has 32 heavy atoms, aromatic amino/phenol regions, halogens, an azetidine ring, aminomethyl and methylaminoethyl side chains. Its central sulfur is written with double bonds to carbon alongside single bonds to aryl and ring nitrogen; this unusual bond environment is not an ordinary sulfone or sulfonamide. Seed 0 reaches a 32-heavy-atom aryl sulfinamide with an aminomethyl-bearing side chain, substituted cyclopentadiene and anisidine-like aromatic region. Seed 1 reaches a 34-heavy-atom densely bridged nitrogen-rich structure with imino/amino groups and an N-S-aryl connection. Mean proposal SMILES length is 63.2, and every proposal contains rings, aromatic atoms and halogen text. Available primary/secondary amines and substantial aromatic regions are already present; their local surroundings and accessibility differ from the Parent's simpler aryl/tertiary-amine leaders.
liabilities: The carbon-multiply-bonded sulfur centre has unestablished stability and synthetic accessibility; it must not be described as a routine sulfone simply because sulfur is present.

Other leaders contain N-S bonds, a substituted cyclopentadiene or highly constrained bridges, requiring environment-specific chemical assessment. The sulfinamide functional group itself is a recognizable class.
Halogen loading, multiple amines and unassigned stereochemistry coexist; the supplied score does not assess their full physical-property or selectivity consequences.
missing_features: The leading examples do not establish conventional alternatives to the unusual sulfur centre and crowded bridges while retaining the favorable amine/aromatic arrangement.
Stereochemical identity and accessible three-dimensional presentation of the saturated and bridged centres are unresolved.
Neutral strings leave protonation representation unspecified, but the molecules visibly contain basic centres; adding nitrogen indiscriminately is not an evidence-supported diagnosis.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: A large sulfonamide/carboxylic-acid-containing early proposal scores 0.009976648048984032. The seed-2 amine-rich sulfur-centred leader scores 0.9509725762830746; replacing one or both aryl chlorines with fluorine, or exchanging phenol for thiol in one related variant, leaves that score unchanged. Removing the terminal amine methyl group gives 0.9390656694874889. The visible favorable association is an arrangement of available aliphatic amines and aromatic regions, with several tolerated peripheral choices, not a requirement for a particular heavy halogen. Seed-0 and seed-1 leaders score 0.9450058947206358 and 0.9418171017577063. All remain below their matched Parent leaders, which score 0.9999989177995104, 0.9969753164881906 and 0.9999934235240012 and present more conventional flexible or cyclic aryl-amine arrangements. This does not prove that sulfur causes the loss, and none of these scores establishes measured binding or selectivity.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 leader has 37 heavy atoms and links a propyl/ethoxy phenyl ring to a densely bridged nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl system incorporating another phenyl ring, tertiary amine and ether connectivity. Other near-leaders alter bridge length, oxygen insertion or nitrogen placement while retaining that large framework. Seed 0 and seed 1 instead retain diaryl fused nitrogen-dione systems with additional nitrogen/alkyl ring closures, with leading sizes of 33 and 35 heavy atoms. Mean proposal SMILES length is 57.9; every proposal has ring and aromatic features, while halogen incidence is only 0.108. Recognizable amine and lactam-like functionality is plentiful, but crowded bridge geometry and synthesis remain unresolved. The seed-2 leader is larger and more extensively connected than the Parent's 29-heavy-atom quinoline/bridged-dicarbonyl leader.
liabilities: Crowded ring junctions and unsaturation within multiply connected ring systems create geometric and synthetic questions despite recognizable constituent functional groups.
Some nearby variants insert N-O or N-N connections, and every proposal lacks stereocentre markers. Graph identity alone does not specify the resulting stereochemical or conformational entity.
missing_features: The larger favorable bridged arrangement lacks demonstrated accessible conformations, stereochemical identity and a practical construction route.
Simpler independent connectivities presenting the favorable aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl relationships at the leading score are not demonstrated.
The improvement in one seed does not establish that indiscriminately adding atoms, bridges or heteroatoms is useful, nor does it identify a missing exact target motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: An early fluorinated aryl-dione proposal scores 0.15402959422966314 and the initial dione scores 0.1678386594791329. The seed-2 bridged family reaches 0.23381705561219815 before a related oxygen-inserted bridge gives 0.23896380545969872. A nearby nitrogen-bridge variant scores 0.23675463149560733. The score ordering associates a combined aromatic, nitrogen and dicarbonyl organization with improvement, without isolating a universal requirement for more bridges. The Child seed-2 leader exceeds the Parent's 0.22600312875247064, an explicit counterexample to uniform decline and to a universal size penalty. Child seed-0 and seed-1 leaders score 0.2123952706490988 and 0.21489069424059337, below Parent 0.2258403994203931 and 0.2214095461892601. The final seed-2 proposal scores 0.22820067810141142, so it is not the incumbent. Low optimizer scores here still belong to full aromatic dione molecules, not tiny fragments.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader has 29 heavy atoms: an N-methyl fused nitrogen-dione core bearing a fluoromethyl ether and attached to a fluorinated benzene fused to an N-C-O-containing saturated ring. It has neither an N-F bond nor the Parent seed-2 leader's small cyclic cumulene. Equally scoring relatives use an N-O-containing fused ring and redistribute fluoroalkyl substitution. The fluoromethyl ether contains an O-C-F sequence, not a direct O-F bond. Seed 0 retains an aromatic-labelled expanded nitrogen ring with imino/carbonyl groups, N-F, fluoroalkene and an aryl ester; seed 2 reaches a compact but extensively annulated nitrogen-dione/azaaryl framework with N-F and phenol. Mean proposal SMILES length is 52.8, halogen incidence 0.8241 and cumulated-double-bond incidence 0.0345. The seed-1 leader has a more recognizable ring topology than the Parent's strongest cyclic-cumulene family, but its saturated heteroatom-rich ring and unresolved stereochemistry still need chemical assessment.
liabilities: N-F and N-S substitutions persist in other seed families even though the leading seed-1 family avoids N-F.
Direct N-O bonds occur in tied seed-1 relatives, while the first leader instead contains N-C-O connectivity; these environments should not be conflated.
Expanded aromatic-labelled nitrogen rings, crowded annulations and some cumulated-double-bond output remain. Text aromaticity and a positive score cannot establish stable three-dimensional geometry.
missing_features: Stable and geometrically credible independent arrangements retaining the favorable fluorinated dione/polar organization are not consistently reached across seeds; the N-F-free seed-1 leader is a positive counterexample to complete dependence on reactive N-halogen chemistry.
Stereochemical definition of fluorinated saturated centres and conformational/tautomeric definition of expanded imino heterocycles are unresolved.
The scores do not identify an exact missing target scaffold or establish that recovering the Parent's chemically doubtful unsaturation is a desirable chemical solution.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. The seed-1 leader and two closely related ring/side-chain variants reach 0.5102212569858039. Removing one aryl fluorine from the N-C-O-ring leader gives 0.47849899583170147, a local association within that scaffold rather than a universal fluorination rule. In seed 0, replacing a ring carbonyl oxygen by sulfur on the otherwise unchanged leading framework takes 0.4381994809951625 to 0.00017893429131171773; maintaining atom count or general scaffold appearance is insufficient. A much larger linked heterocyclic proposal scores 4.8036238775944616e-27, and difluoromethane scores 1.409300415191629e-22, showing poor outcomes at both size extremes. The Child seed-1 leader exceeds its Parent's 0.4870057305679067, whereas Child seed-0 and seed-2 leaders at 0.4381994809951625 and 0.3077866564136952 fall below Parent 0.6510211907030741 and 0.7208853668418119. The latter Parent leader has doubtful cyclic-cumulene geometry; its higher score is not a reason to declare that chemistry desirable.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-299096e31fe7, compared with complete code Parent n-62daf219c70a on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied current profile and 300 observations per task. The Parent reactivity gap, originally recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c, persists but changes form: current leaders include N-halogenated amidines/hydrazides, consecutive oxygen chains and carbon-multiply-bonded sulfur. Counterexamples include a conventional indole anilide, a recognizable sulfinamide and a fluorinated N-C-O-ring leader without N-F. These observations concern local environments, not an inability to make stable heterocycles or useful amines.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently preserve conventional bond environments when decorating otherwise recognizable aromatic and heterocyclic frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations need environment-sensitive chemical alternatives that preserve feedback-supported functional-group relationships while distinguishing ordinary carbon-bound halogens, ethers and sulfur functions from unusual bond patterns. Blanket bans on halogens, nitrogen or sulfur would ignore the counterexamples. No score benefit from filtering or replacing any one environment is established, and this chemistry association does not attribute the liability to the registered component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-299096e31fe7 under the complete current-profile comparison with n-62daf219c70a, Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per task. A leading oxygen-rich assembly has 65 heavy atoms versus its matched Parent leader's 30, while another family has fifteen same-score variants changing oxygen chains, ester groups and related decorations. Leaders within seeds commonly retain a framework despite these edits. Yet a 37-heavy-atom bridged family exceeds its matched 29-heavy-atom Parent leader, and distinct seed families remain. The Parent's general context-loss/coverage concern therefore persists mainly as elaboration and limited alternatives here, not widespread fragmentation.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits substantial peripheral elaboration without consistently finding compact independent ways to preserve the favorable functional-group arrangement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Proposals should test chemically independent or simpler connectivities that retain learned useful aromatic, polar and basic regions, and use local feedback to distinguish meaningful alternatives from score-equivalent decorations. Preserve the possibility that a larger framework is useful. Neither a fixed size cutoff nor a general preference for more diversity follows from these data; the current output establishes a conditional coverage gap, not a causal diagnosis of allocation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-299096e31fe7 and its complete Parent comparison under the supplied Search profile and budget. Current leaders include crowded nitrogen-ring bridges, a substituted cyclopentadiene, extensively annulated diones and an expanded aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring. The Parent geometry concern originated in n-c55c3d520a2c and was retained in n-62daf219c70a, but its specific strongest cyclic-cumulene leader should not be imputed to the Child. A more conventional saturated N-C-O-ring family is a current counterexample, and the larger bridged family can improve its supplied score despite unresolved geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently establish geometric feasibility when creating dense bridges, small unsaturated rings or expanded aromatic-labelled heterocycles.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need checks or alternatives sensitive to actual connectivity, unsaturation and conformational constraints, rather than ring count or aromatic text alone. Maintain recognizable small and fused rings where appropriate. The evidence does not show that every bridge is inaccessible or that rejecting difficult topologies necessarily improves score; synthesis and geometry remain separate chemical uncertainties.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-299096e31fe7 on all supplied Search Seeds at 300 observations per task, continuing the gap recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced in Parent n-62daf219c70a. Every current task has stereocentre-string incidence 0.0, while aryl-bearing saturated centres, fluorinated heterocycles, sulfinamide and bridged nitrogen frameworks contain potential stereochemical distinctions. Formal-charge incidence is also 0.0, but obvious primary and secondary amines remain; lack of charged notation is not lack of protonatable chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not provide explicit stereochemical identity for the saturated and bridged structures it emits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representations and transformations need to preserve or deliberately resolve relevant stereochemistry while distinguishing stable stereoisomers from achiral or configurationally labile cases. Protonation, tautomerism and imine geometry require separate treatment where relevant. These output records establish incomplete chemical identity, not a measured score penalty, and do not prove that adding charge or stereochemical enumeration would improve the objective.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Task-local finite accepted archive, score-quantile breeding-parent selection and bounded greedy survival.
Connected-fragment crossover with the unchanged post-crossover mutation probability and ordinary mutation continuation.
Ordinary replace/append/delete/insert/bond-change/ring-open/ring-close edits, walk rules, saturation laws and retry limits; direct aromatic C/N exchange remains disabled.
Sanitization, stable canonical identity admission, initial/emitted and temporary-pool duplicate rejection, and fixed 160-member surplus pools.
Integer-count Morgan representation, generalized Tanimoto kernel, accepted-only chronological GP fitting, normalization, fixed observation noise and jitter.
Full posterior covariance, Cholesky, original single normal-array draw, correlated sampled arrays and finite/failure checks, retained as passive successful-allocation controls.
Stable available posterior-mean allocation, exact actual pool/emission/pending prediction joins and next-fit probes; inherited generation-order numerical fallback remains.
Passive independently masked sampled-rule comparator, aromatic-pair enumeration and unreachable exchange implementation, preserving visible computational complexity.
Fresh objective-local state, unchanged prepared configuration and exact protocol-owned batches, seeds, budgets and resources.
